findings_qualitative.value: Cloud lies between Galactic and extragalactic clouds in SFR-Mgas and Sigma_g-Sigma_SFR diagrams; consistent with turbulence-regulated star formation

evidence.quote: We found that the gas stands a unique position between galactic and extraglactic clouds

claims.hypothesis: The 689 GHz peak near S1 is a distinct massive dense gas cloud
claims.experiment: Analysis of archival Band 9 continuum and CO(6-5) cubes plus grey-body SED and RADEX
claims.result: Mgas ~(2-5)e5 Msun, size ~10 pc, n~1e5 cm-3, SFR~0.1 Msun/yr
claims.finding: A proto star cluster forming cloud 14 pc from S1

evidence.quote: We therefore refer to the gas as “massive dense gas cloud"

claims.hypothesis: Gas inflow to the nucleus was driven by a past minor merger
claims.experiment: Qualitative comparison with literature on decoupled nuclear dynamics
claims.finding: Minor merger proposed as most natural mechanism

evidence.loc: 5.2 Origin of the Massive Dense Gas Cloud
evidence.quote: the gas fueling driven by minor-merger seems to be the most natural mechanism for the case of NGC 1068

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single static opaque gas with self-absorption rejected because no double-peaked profile with central dip

evidence.loc: 3.2 Molecular Gas Associated with the 689 GHz Continuum Peak

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pure rotation rejected due to too high specific angular momentum

evidence.quote: we argue that the gas is not in equilibrium by a pure rotation

limitations_admitted.value: Beam does not resolve the cloud; higher resolution and sensitivity needed
